description: An EXECUTED Heritage `output` escaping at the top level carries the CANONICAL `params.keyword` `"return"` (issue #741). `output` is a Heritage alternate spelling of Core `return` (`spec/conformance.md#heritage` — "alternate spellings only, no new semantics"), lowered onto the same `Return` node, so the two are ONE condition and must carry ONE machine-readable identity: `code`, `params`, `stage` and `severity` here are byte-identical to the Core twin `tests/conformance/core-language/execution/procedure-return-outside-proc` (`return 1` at top level), which reports the same `params` `{ keyword: "return" }` at `stage: "semantic"`. Diagnostic identity is `code` plus structured `params` and the same condition MUST keep the same params (`spec/error-model.md:255-260`). The runtime keeps its own copy of the checker's control-flow rule, for a caller driving `evaluate()`/`createEnvironment()` directly (issue #815 put a checker in front of `execute()`, so a checked run reports the checker's copy and de-duplicates the runtime's) — and that copy still emitted the surface spelling after the checker was canonicalized in #737, so the same program reported `keyword: "output"` when executed and `keyword: "return"` when checked. The semantic-stage twin `heritage/check/heritage-return-alias-canonical-keyword-outside-proc` now agrees on identity — same `code`, same `params` — and, since issue #815, on `stage` as well — the checker's copy is the one a checked run delivers. The two producers still span differently by design (the checker the control word, the runtime the whole statement, as it does for Core `return` too), which is why `mergeRunDiagnostics` folds them on overlapping spans rather than on identical ones. The prose `message` still names the learner's own word (`output …`) — that is the localization boundary and is permitted. The event stream is empty, exactly as the Core spelling's is: the escape is decided statically, so the program does not run. Under the `runUnchecked` opt-out both spellings still emit their `instruction` and `return` events before the diagnostic. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy does not appear beside the check's.
